checks: No eclipse at 12 of 32 covered epochs where the 2.14255 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 273787849 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.1425 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse causing the star to dim by 2.80%, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 402.7 using box least-squares analysis. No secondary eclipse was observed. Pixel-level image analysis confirms the dimming occurs at the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise of 36.4, though the centroid offset of 10.1 arcsec warrants attention. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The automated pipeline's machine-learning classifier assigned a score of 0.77 (on a scale where 1 indicates highest confidence), and the data passed all quality checks without flags.
